decision: The text was drafted from the Consistency classes of a private A/B defect catalogue of one Rust change. The skill is not measured on that same change.

evidence.text: Requirement of the drafting brief for backlog item 47: record the provenance and the exclusion in each skill of the family.

reopen_if: Never for that change. Any other change, in any language, is a valid workpiece.
why: The catalogue holds the confirmed defects of that change, so an arm that loads this skill there would be reading the judges' answers, and its score would say nothing about the skill.

anchors: Writing it into your own notes does not make it part of the spec.
decision: An author never ships a condition the spec does not carry (a minimum sample, a cooldown, a fallback), even when it is written into the author's own notes; the specified behaviour ships and the proposal goes to the spec's owner as a question.

evidence.text: Headless implementer probe on a planted Python service (tasks adding an alert beside existing figures, with a product-owner note about a flapping alert): RED haiku 2 of 2 gate added, opus 0 of 2; GREEN haiku 0 of 3, opus 0 of 1.

reopen_if: A project wants authors to ship a recorded departure without the owner's answer, or a measurement on a real plan shows the rule holding back changes the owner wanted.
why: It is the one behaviour the baseline failed on: without the skill a haiku implementer under a stakeholder's request added a minimum-sample gate of 20 in 2 of 2 runs and recorded it only in its own notes; with the skill 0 of 3 haiku runs and 0 of 1 opus runs added one, and each raised the owner question instead.

anchors: review that lists findings without it has not shown what was compared.
decision: A review under this lens returns the pair table (one row per pair, set / rule / window / unit, a verdict per row) together with the findings.

evidence.text: GREEN reviewer probes, opus and haiku, on three scenarios (9, 11 and 15 planted defects): every arm returned the table with AGREE, DISAGREE, ONE-SIDED and ADDED verdicts and lost no finding against RED.

reopen_if: Reviewers on real changes find the table too long to fill, or a consumer of reviews needs a different format.
why: The table is what the skill adds for a reviewer: it shows which pairs were compared and found to agree, which a findings list cannot. With the skill every reviewer arm returned it and findings carried a concrete input (10 of 15 findings for haiku on the large scenario against 1 without the skill).

anchors: Whether each side is correct in isolation is a different review.
decision: The lens compares two places with each other; whether one place is correct in isolation is left to other reviews.

evidence.text: Grouping of the 20 source classes by mechanism: 6 two-path or two-population, 3 windows, 6 spec departures (2 of them added conditions), 3 prose, 1 interface, 1 literal standing for a held value; 0 about names or types.

reopen_if: The lens definition used by the review experiments changes, or a later catalogue shows name or type disagreements as a class of its own.
why: It keeps the lens apart from a correctness review and from the spec-compliance review that process-agents-subagent-driven-development already runs; the definition handed to reviewers (names, types and behaviour agree) matched none of the source classes on names or types, so the skill is built on the pairings the classes do show.

decision: The skill text and its description make no claim that a reviewer finds more consistency defects with it than without.

evidence.text: RED reviewer probes, opus and haiku: small Go 9/9 and 9/9, Python 11/11 and 10/11, Rust 11/11 and 11/11, large Python (13 files, 15 planted) 15/15 twice on each tier.

reopen_if: A measurement on a change of real plan size (not the source change) shows reviewers missing consistency defects without the skill and finding them with it.
why: Measured baselines left no headroom: reviewers told only the lens name found 9 of 9, 11 of 11 and 15 of 15 planted defects on opus, and haiku missed 1 of 11 once, on scenarios up to 13 files.
